correctness.rationale: For every n>=6, the induced subcomplexes supported on three consecutive rungs are contractible cones; they cover all cliques including the only projected exceptional triangle obstruction at n=6, all nonempty intersections are full simplices, and their nerve collapses by n free-edge/triangle pairs to C_n. For n=3,4 diameter two gives a simplex; for n=5 each of the 48 supplied collapse pairs is replayed against the original graph-square face set, leaving exactly an octahedral S2. Twenty exact signed simplicial Lefschetz calculations establish the exceptional integral sign character; the equivariant nerve projection determines the stable character. Scale-one Betti rank and map surjectivity follow from graph counts and filled two-edge detours. Bounded finite tests are not used to prove the unbounded case.

originality.rationale: The archive-era graph-power theory does not cover these square graphs: its girth-based theorem excludes graph 4-cycles, and its closed-neighborhood clique containment condition fails for adjacent-rung four-cliques. The closest full-text published prism and Cartesian clique-fiber results use untwisted Cartesian graph products, while the graph here is a twisted cyclic ladder; in particular the stable threshold and exceptional n=6 differ. Metric gluing/continuous circular ladders use other spaces or metrics, and Möbius-ladder independence, neighborhood and matching complexes use different face conditions. published-finding corpus searches under power-graph, Rips, twisted ladder, circular ladder, dihedral character and small exception aliases found no prior statement implying the combined all-n integral theorem. Overlap with an unindexed calculation remains a risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent unindexed, unpublished or alternative-named graph-square calculations cannot be ruled out by indexed searches.
The dihedral orientation character for this particular Rips complex might appear in an equivariant-topology source not returned by targeted indexing.

value.rationale: The Möbius ladder is a canonical cubic cyclic family, and integer scale two is its first nontrivial Rips thickening. A complete integral classification for every rung count has a sharp small exception at n=5 and a stable circle already at n=6, in contrast to the untwisted prism. The integral dihedral orientation action and survival of exactly one first-persistence class supply structural information beyond enumerations. The question is a coherent natural graph-family classification rather than a parameter-picked slice.
